assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data transformed the measurement and analysis of intergenerational mobility and made inequality of opportunity a central empirical research agenda.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren, and Friedman are central architects of the linked-data mobility research program.
assessment.maturity: The findings, data infrastructure, and ensuing research program are extensively developed and influential.
uncertainties: The evidence is concentrated in particular institutional settings and causal interpretation of place effects remains demanding.
The appropriate boundary between this contribution and related inequality research is contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work fundamentally clarified how technology, tasks, and trade shocks reshape labour demand, local adjustment, and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson made distinctive, mutually reinforcing contributions to the empirical framework and its application to trade exposure.
assessment.maturity: The research has generated a large subsequent literature and remains highly relevant to labour-market change.
uncertainties: Attribution across the broader task, trade, and wage-inequality literatures is necessarily difficult.
Estimated effects can depend on exposure measures and adjustment horizons.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The integration of adverse-selection theory with credible empirical measurement materially changed insurance economics and policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: Finkelstein, Einav, and Salanie are prominent contributors to the theoretical and empirical foundations of this program.
assessment.maturity: The framework has been tested across insurance markets and has had durable influence on health and public economics.
uncertainties: The candidate grouping covers a broad literature with several additional important contributors.
External validity varies across insurance institutions and products.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on early-life conditions connected health shocks, human-capital formation, and later-life outcomes in a consequential and coherent body of evidence.
assessment.attribution: Currie, Almond, and Cunha represent complementary empirical and conceptual contributions to the field.
assessment.maturity: The agenda has accumulated evidence across cohorts, settings, and developmental stages.
uncertainties: The broad early-life field makes a sharply bounded prize contribution challenging.
Some mechanisms and policy extrapolations remain context dependent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification provided a principled way to draw credible conclusions when data and assumptions cannot justify point identification.
assessment.attribution: Manski established the foundational approach, with Tamer and Molinari making major advances in moment inequalities and implementation.
assessment.maturity: The methods are well established and have spread across econometrics and applied economics.
uncertainties: The contribution is methodologically broad, making its most appropriate laureate set debatable.
Its practical impact is less readily summarized by a single empirical application.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Audit and correspondence studies supplied compelling evidence on labour-market discrimination and reshaped empirical work on unequal treatment.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan produced a landmark correspondence experiment, while Charles has made central contributions to the broader discrimination literature.
assessment.maturity: The approach has been replicated, extended, and incorporated into labour-market research and policy debate.
uncertainties: Audit designs identify treatment at an initial stage but do not by themselves characterize all mechanisms of discrimination.
Credit extends to important methodological and substantive predecessors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The modern analysis of monopsony restored employer market power to the centre of labour economics and changed evaluation of wages and labour-market policy.
assessment.attribution: Manning supplied a foundational synthesis and theory, while Ashenfelter and Naidu have made influential empirical and institutional contributions.
assessment.maturity: The research has become central to current labour economics and has generated substantial empirical confirmation.
uncertainties: The candidate combines foundational and more recent strands with a broad set of potential contributors.
The magnitude and forms of employer power differ markedly across markets.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Empirical work on taxable-income responses and optimal taxation greatly improved the evidence base for tax design and distributional policy.
assessment.attribution: Saez, Slemrod, and Chetty have made major, distinct contributions to measurement, behavioral responses, and tax-policy analysis.
assessment.maturity: The literature is mature, widely used, and influential in both public economics and policy design.
uncertainties: Elasticity estimates depend on tax institutions, avoidance opportunities, and policy context.
The contribution overlaps with a large surrounding literature on inequality and public finance.
